learn: Scarcity means unlimited wants but limited resources.
Factors of production: land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship.
Every society must decide what, how and for whom to produce.
lessons.try: List the factors of production for a pizza shop.

learn: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative given up.
Every choice involves trade-offs.
Thinking at the margin compares one more unit's costs and benefits.
check: Opportunity cost is the next best...
lessons.try: Calculate the opportunity cost of a weekend job.

learn: Traditional, command, market and mixed economies.
The US is a mixed market economy.
Production possibilities curves show trade-offs and efficiency.
lessons.try: Draw a production possibilities curve for two goods.

learn: The law of demand: as price rises, quantity demanded falls.
Demand shifts with income, tastes, prices of related goods, expectations and number of buyers.
Elastic demand changes a lot with price; inelastic changes little.
check: A rise in income usually ___ demand for normal goods.
lessons.try: Graph a demand curve from a class survey.

learn: The law of supply: as price rises, quantity supplied rises.
Supply shifts with input costs, technology, taxes and number of sellers.
Better technology increases supply.
lessons.try: Explain how a drought affects the supply of wheat.

learn: Equilibrium is where supply meets demand.
Shortages occur below equilibrium price; surpluses above.
Price ceilings (rent control) and floors (minimum wage) affect markets.
check: A price below equilibrium causes a...
lessons.try: Model how a new trend shifts equilibrium.

learn: Sole proprietorships, partnerships, corporations and LLCs.
Corporations offer limited liability; owners risk only their investment.
Non-profits serve missions instead of profits.
check: A business owned by one person is a...
lessons.try: Compare the pros and cons of each business type.

learn: Perfect competition, monopolistic competition, oligopoly and monopoly.
More competition usually means lower prices and more choice.
Antitrust laws limit monopolies.
check: A market with a few large firms is an...
lessons.try: Classify ten markets by structure.

learn: Wages are set by supply and demand for labour.
Education and skills raise earning potential.
Unions bargain collectively for workers.
check: Wages are set by supply and ___ for labour.
lessons.try: Research wages and training for three careers.

learn: GDP is the market value of all final goods and services produced in a country in a year.
Real GDP adjusts for inflation; GDP per capita divides by population.
GDP leaves out unpaid work and environmental costs.
check: GDP per capita divides GDP by...
lessons.try: Compare GDP per capita for five countries.

learn: The unemployment rate counts people looking for work who can't find it.
Inflation is a general rise in prices, measured by the Consumer Price Index.
Moderate inflation (about 2%) is a common target.
check: CPI rising from 200 to 206 is ___ inflation.
A common inflation target is about...
lessons.try: Calculate inflation from two years of CPI data.

learn: Phases: expansion, peak, contraction (recession), trough.
A recession is a significant decline in economic activity.
The Great Depression and the 2008 crisis were severe downturns.
check: A recession is a period of...
The lowest point of the cycle is the...
lessons.try: Label the business cycle on a graph of real GDP.

learn: Money is a medium of exchange, store of value and unit of account.
Modern money is fiat: valuable because people trust it.
Money supply includes cash and bank deposits.
check: A unit of account lets us...
lessons.try: Explain why a dollar bill has value.

learn: Banks accept deposits and lend money, earning interest.
Deposits in insured banks are protected by the FDIC up to $250,000.
Credit unions are member-owned.
check: The FDIC insures deposits up to...
lessons.try: Compare a bank and a credit union account.

learn: The Fed is the US central bank.
It raises interest rates to cool inflation and lowers them to boost growth.
Open market operations buy and sell government securities.
lessons.try: Follow a Fed announcement and its effects.

learn: Progressive taxes take a higher share from higher incomes (federal income tax).
Regressive taxes take a larger share from lower incomes (sales taxes in effect).
Taxes fund roads, schools, defence and social programmes; FICA payroll taxes fund Social Security and Medicare.
lessons.try: Read a sample pay stub and identify each deduction.

learn: Fiscal policy uses government spending and taxes to influence the economy.
A deficit is when spending exceeds revenue in a year; the debt is the total owed.
Stimulus spending can boost a weak economy.
lessons.try: Analyse the federal budget by category.

learn: Comparative advantage: countries specialise in what they produce at lowest opportunity cost.
Tariffs tax imports; quotas limit them.
Exchange rates affect trade.
check: Specialising by lowest opportunity cost is...
A tariff is a tax on...
lessons.try: Trace where five products you own were made.

learn: Income comes from wages, salaries, tips, self-employment and investments.
Gross pay is before deductions; net pay is take-home.
Form W-4 sets tax withholding; W-2 reports annual wages.
check: $15 an hour for 20 hours is ___ gross.
lessons.try: Calculate net pay from a gross paycheck.

learn: A budget plans income and expenses.
The 50/30/20 guideline: 50% needs, 30% wants, 20% saving and debt repayment.
Track spending to find leaks.
lessons.try: Build a monthly budget for a first apartment.

learn: Short-, medium- and long-term goals.
An emergency fund covers 3-6 months of expenses.
Pay yourself first by saving automatically.
check: An emergency fund covers about ___ months.
Buying a house is a ___ goal.
lessons.try: Set three SMART financial goals.

learn: Compound interest earns interest on interest.
Rule of 72: years to double ≈ 72 ÷ interest rate.
Starting early matters most.
check: At 6%, money doubles in about ___ years.
The most important factor is starting...
lessons.try: Compare saving from age 20 versus age 30.

learn: Stocks (ownership), bonds (loans) and mutual funds or index funds (baskets).
Higher potential return usually means higher risk.
Diversification spreads risk.
lessons.try: Build a pretend diversified portfolio.

learn: 401(k)s and IRAs offer tax advantages; employer matches are free money.
Index funds offer low fees and broad diversification.
Avoid "guaranteed high returns" scams and pressure tactics.
lessons.try: Identify warning signs in three investment offers.

learn: Credit lets you borrow now and pay later with interest.
APR is the yearly cost of borrowing.
Minimum payments keep you in debt longer and cost more.
check: APR is the yearly cost of...
lessons.try: Calculate the cost of paying only the minimum on a card.

learn: Scores (300-850) depend on payment history, amounts owed, history length, new credit and credit mix.
Payment history matters most.
Check your free credit reports regularly.
check: The biggest credit score factor is...
lessons.try: Explain three ways to build good credit.

learn: Federal student loans usually have lower rates and more protections than private loans.
Compare total cost, not just monthly payment.
Avoid payday loans with very high fees.
check: Federal student loans usually have ___ rates.
lessons.try: Compare the costs of three ways to pay for college.

units.t: Consumer Protection, Insurance and Big Decisions

learn: Consumers have rights to safety, information, choice and to be heard.
The FTC and CFPB protect consumers from fraud.
Read contracts before signing; know cancellation rights.
lessons.try: Analyse the fine print of a phone contract.

learn: Insurance shares risk: you pay premiums; the insurer pays covered losses.
Deductibles are what you pay first.
Types: health, auto, renters, life, disability.
check: A higher deductible usually means a ___ premium.
lessons.try: Compare two auto insurance quotes.

learn: Renting versus buying: costs, flexibility and equity.
Buying a car: total cost of ownership includes insurance, fuel and repairs.
Use decision-making models to compare options.
lessons.try: Make a decision matrix for a big purchase.
